title: Making a Koszul regular sequence regular after a faithfully flat smooth base change
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a Koszul regular sequence which does not generate the unit ideal becomes a regular sequence after the faithfully flat smooth extension obtained by adjoining an invertible triangular matrix of variables, and that the ideals generated stay equal. The proof observes that the triangular matrix is invertible, so the equality of ideals is immediate, then uses the vanishing of the top Koszul homology to see that the kernel of multiplication by the sequence is zero, applies the nonzerodivisor criterion to the first new element, records that the new first element together with the remaining old ones is again Koszul regular, truncates to get Koszul regularity of the remaining images in the quotient, and concludes by induction on the length of the sequence.
